# BUPATI PASURUAN REGULATION
NUMBER 71 OF 2016

CONCERNING

AMENDMENT TO BUPATI PASURUAN REGULATION NUMBER 63 OF 2014 CONCERNING POSITION, ORGANIZATIONAL STRUCTURE, DUTIES AND FUNCTIONS AS WELL AS WORK PROCEDURES OF THE REGIONAL SECRETARIAT AND SECRETARIAT OF THE REGIONAL PEOPLE'S REPRESENTATIVE COUNCIL

WITH THE BLESSING OF GOD ALMIGHTY

BUPATI PASURUAN,

Considering : a. that in order to implement the provisions of Article 4 paragraph (2) of Government Regulation Number 18 of 2016 concerning Regional Apparatus, it is necessary to adjust the nomenclature of the Regional Secretariat organizational structure;

b. that based on the considerations as referred to in letter a, it is necessary to stipulate a Bupati Regulation concerning Amendment to Bupati Pasuruan Regulation Number 63 of 2014 concerning Position, Organizational Structure, Duties and Functions as well as Work Procedures of the Regional Secretariat and Secretariat of the Regional People's Representative Council;

In view of : 1. Law Number 12 of 1950 concerning Establishment of Autonomous Regions and Autonomous Cities within East Java Province (State Gazette of the Republic of Indonesia of 1950 Number 41, Supplement to State Gazette of the Republic of Indonesia Number 9);

2. Law Number 5 of 2014 concerning State Civil Apparatus (State Gazette of the Republic of Indonesia of 2014 Number 6, Supplement to State Gazette of the Republic of Indonesia Number 5494);

3. Law Number 23 of 2014 concerning Regional Government (State Gazette of the Republic of Indonesia of 2014 Number 244, Supplement to State Gazette of the Republic of Indonesia Number 5587) as amended several times, most recently by Law Number 9 of 2015 concerning Second Amendment to Law Number 23 of 2014 concerning Regional Government (State Gazette of the Republic of Indonesia of 2015 Number 58, Supplement to State Gazette of the Republic of Indonesia Number 5679);

4. Government Regulation Number 18 of 2016 concerning Regional Apparatus (State Gazette of the Republic of Indonesia of 2016 Number 114, Supplement to State Gazette of the Republic of Indonesia Number 5887);

5. Bupati Pasuruan Regulation Number 63 of 2014 concerning Position, Organizational Structure, Duties and Functions as well as Work Procedures of the Regional Secretariat and Secretariat of the Regional People's Representative Council (Regional Gazette of Pasuruan Regency of 2014 Number 4 Series E);

HAS DECIDED:

To stipulate : BUPATI REGULATION CONCERNING AMENDMENT TO BUPATI PASURUAN REGULATION NUMBER 63 OF 2014 CONCERNING POSITION, ORGANIZATIONAL STRUCTURE, DUTIES AND FUNCTIONS AS WELL AS WORK PROCEDURES OF THE REGIONAL SECRETARIAT AND SECRETARIAT OF THE REGIONAL PEOPLE'S REPRESENTATIVE COUNCIL.

Article I

Several provisions in Bupati Pasuruan Regulation Number 63 of 2014 concerning Position, Organizational Structure, Duties and Functions as well as Work Procedures of the Regional Secretariat and Secretariat of the Regional People's Representative Council (Regional Gazette of Pasuruan Regency of 2014 Number 4 Series E) are amended as follows:

1. The provisions of Article 1 number 11 are amended so that Article 1 reads as follows:

Article 1

In this Bupati Regulation, what is meant by:
1. Region is Pasuruan Regency.
2. Regional Government is the Bupati as an element of regional government administration who leads the implementation of government affairs which are the authority of the autonomous region.
3. Bupati is the Bupati of Pasuruan.
4. Regional People's Representative Council, hereinafter abbreviated as DPRD, is the Regional People's Representative Council of Pasuruan Regency.
5. Regional Secretariat is the Regional Secretariat of Pasuruan Regency.
6. Regional Secretary is the Regional Secretary of Pasuruan Regency.
7. DPRD Secretariat is the Secretariat of the Regional People's Representative Council of Pasuruan Regency.
8. DPRD Secretary is the Secretary of the Regional People's Representative Council of Pasuruan Regency.
9. Assistant is an Assistant at the Regional Secretariat of Pasuruan Regency.
10. Bureau is a Bureau at the Regional Secretariat of Pasuruan Regency.
11. Division is a Division at the DPRD Secretariat of Pasuruan Regency.
12. Sub-bureau is a Sub-bureau at the Regional Secretariat of Pasuruan Regency.
13. Sub-division is a Sub-division at the DPRD Secretariat of Pasuruan Regency.
14. Functional Group is a group of civil servants who occupy functional positions.

2. The provisions of Article 4 paragraph (1) letter b are amended, so that Article 4 reads as follows:

Article 4

(1) Regional Secretariat has the following duties:
a. assisting the Bupati in formulating policies and coordinating Regional Apparatus; and
b. providing administrative services and support to all Regional Apparatus within the regional government.

(2) In carrying out the duties as referred to in paragraph (1), the Regional Secretariat performs the following functions:
a. coordination of policy formulation;
b. coordination of policy implementation;
c. monitoring and evaluation of policy implementation;
d. administrative services;
e. fostering of Regional Secretariat organizational units;
f. implementation of other duties assigned by the Bupati in accordance with their duties and functions; and
g. implementation of Regional Secretariat administrative and household affairs.

3. The provisions of Article 6 paragraph (2) letter b are amended, so that Article 6 reads as follows:

Article 6

(1) Assistant for Government and People's Welfare is under and responsible to the Regional Secretary.

(2) Assistant for Government and People's Welfare has the following duties:
a. assisting the Regional Secretary in coordinating the formulation of policies in the fields of government, law, community and village empowerment, population and civil registration, education and culture, health, social affairs, women's empowerment and family planning, as well as food security; and
b. assisting the Regional Secretary in coordinating Regional Apparatus in the fields of government, law, community and village empowerment, population and civil registration, education and culture, health, social affairs, women's empowerment and family planning, as well as food security.

(3) In carrying out the duties as referred to in paragraph (2), the Assistant for Government and People's Welfare performs the following functions:
a. coordination of policy formulation in the fields of government, law, community and village empowerment, population and civil registration, education and culture, health, social affairs, women's empowerment and family planning, as well as food security;
b. coordination of Regional Apparatus in the fields of government, law, community and village empowerment, population and civil registration, education and culture, health, social affairs, women's empowerment and family planning, as well as food security;
c. monitoring and evaluation of policy implementation in the fields of government, law, community and village empowerment, population and civil registration, education and culture, health, social affairs, women's empowerment and family planning, as well as food security;
d. implementation of other duties assigned by the Regional Secretary in accordance with their duties and functions; and
e. implementation of administrative affairs of the Assistant for Government and People's Welfare.

4. The provisions of Article 7 paragraph (2) letter b are amended, so that Article 7 reads as follows:

Article 7

(1) Assistant for Economy and Development is under and responsible to the Regional Secretary.

(2) Assistant for Economy and Development has the following duties:
a. assisting the Regional Secretary in coordinating the formulation of policies in the fields of development, economy, natural resources, cooperatives, micro, small and medium enterprises, investment, one-stop integrated services, as well as tourism, youth and sports; and
b. assisting the Regional Secretary in coordinating Regional Apparatus in the fields of development, economy, natural resources, cooperatives, micro, small and medium enterprises, investment, one-stop integrated services, as well as tourism, youth and sports.

(3) In carrying out the duties as referred to in paragraph (2), the Assistant for Economy and Development performs the following functions:
a. coordination of policy formulation in the fields of development, economy, natural resources, cooperatives, micro, small and medium enterprises, investment, one-stop integrated services, as well as tourism, youth and sports;
b. coordination of Regional Apparatus in the fields of development, economy, natural resources, cooperatives, micro, small and medium enterprises, investment, one-stop integrated services, as well as tourism, youth and sports;
c. monitoring and evaluation of policy implementation in the fields of development, economy, natural resources, cooperatives, micro, small and medium enterprises, investment, one-stop integrated services, as well as tourism, youth and sports;
d. implementation of other duties assigned by the Regional Secretary in accordance with their duties and functions; and
e. implementation of administrative affairs of the Assistant for Economy and Development.

5. The provisions of Article 8 paragraph (2) letter b are amended, so that Article 8 reads as follows:

Article 8

(1) Assistant for Administration is under and responsible to the Regional Secretary.

CONCERNING
WOMEN'S EMPOWERMENT AND CHILD PROTECTION

I. GENERAL

The State as the mandate holder of people's sovereignty is responsible for implementing development to achieve community welfare. This is as mandated by the constitution which has become a national consensus for the Indonesian nation. The 1945 Constitution is the fundamental legal foundation (Fundamental Norm) in formulating the direction and basis for social, political, and state legal policy-making.

The State as an organization certainly always has objectives as stated in the fourth paragraph of the preamble of the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia which states: "Furthermore, to form a Government of the State of the Republic of Indonesia that protects the entire Indonesian nation and all Indonesian territory and to promote general welfare, educate the life of the nation, and participate in implementing world order based on freedom, eternal peace and social justice." Observing the fourth paragraph of the Preamble of the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia, it is clearly stated that this state was formed with the aim of protecting the entire nation and all Indonesian territory as well as improving the welfare of the people. This is also the objective of the formation of regional government which aims to accelerate the realization of community welfare through improvement, services, empowerment, and community participation, as well as increasing regional competitiveness by taking into account the principles of democracy, equity, justice, privileges and specificities of a region within the system of the Unitary State of the Republic of Indonesia.

Explicitly, the objectives of the Indonesian State reflect several national objectives of the Indonesian nation. The objectives contained in this fourth paragraph constitute the constitutional promise of the Indonesian state to all its people while simultaneously becoming the basic rights of the community. Therefore, the State is obligated to make various efforts in order to fulfill the constitutional rights of its citizens.

One of these four objectives is to protect the entire Indonesian nation and all Indonesian territory as well as promote general welfare. This means that the Indonesian nation must be free from all forms of actions that can harm its citizens, efforts to maintain this conduciveness are carried out in order to create a prosperous and beneficial social life without looking at certain groups and classes, because the meaning of the entire nation is a reflection for all Indonesian people without exception, whether men, women or children.

The protection that is the State's responsibility is not only for every person both in the individual and group sense along with the cultural identity attached to them, but this protection must also be interpreted as an endeavor to promote general welfare for the entire nation. Therefore, there need to be steps that must be taken by the State to achieve the above objectives by empowering its people, especially those who have been considered weak and marginalized. Based on these considerations, the Pasuruan Regency Government needs to establish a Regional Regulation on Women's Empowerment and Child Protection as a concrete step in order to protect the entire nation and promote general welfare.

From the above description, it is explicitly explained that based on article 18 of the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia, regional governments have the authority to make regulations related to regional needs in order to accommodate regional potential and local wisdom according to their respective localistic needs. Whereas for Pasuruan Regency, it has a distinctive character as a santri city that is strong with the values of its religious teachings. From the perspective of Islam, women's empowerment and child protection are highly upheld, even when Islam was first revealed to the Prophet Muhammad SAW. The condition of the Arab nation at that time greatly looked down upon the status of women. This can be proven by the existence of the custom of women as wives being able to be inherited to their children if their father died. Furthermore, for the fate of children at that time, it seemed that there was absolutely no protection of the rights given, children born with female gender would be killed by being buried alive because they were considered a disgrace to their parents. Departing from this condition, it is necessary to establish a regulation that reflects the values of women's empowerment and child protection.

Women's empowerment and child protection is a problem that needs to receive special attention from the Pasuruan Regency regional government to immediately create a juridical instrument to guard and ensure the guarantee of welfare and security for women and children.

Therefore, a legal umbrella in the form of a Regional Regulation is needed that is capable of accommodating all issues related to women's empowerment and child protection, capable of providing integrated services holistically and comprehensively, and explicitly giving mandates to institutions to coordinate policies and supervision, and mandates to institutions to provide services. In addition, the Regional Regulation can also open the involvement of non-governmental institutions and the community as well as the business world to play a broad role.

The implementation of women's empowerment and child protection in Pasuruan Regency does not yet have a strong legal basis in the form of regional regulations. Therefore, activities related to women's empowerment and child protection are carried out optimally in order to provide protection for women and children.

In relation to this, the Regional Regulation on women's empowerment and child protection is expected to anticipate and overcome all problems related to women's empowerment and child protection programs as well as become a juridical solution for regulations in Pasuruan Regency, so that it can provide protection and services to women and children in an integrated and comprehensive manner.

Article 1
In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:
1. Region is Pasuruan Regency.
2. Regional Government is the Regional Government of Pasuruan Regency.
3. Regent is the Regent of Pasuruan.
4. Regional Apparatus Organization hereinafter abbreviated as OPD is the Regional Apparatus Organization within the Government of Pasuruan Regency.
5. Child is a person who has not reached the age of 18 (eighteen) years, including a child still in the womb.
6. Woman is a person (human being) who can menstruate, become pregnant, give birth to children and breastfeed.
7. Family is the smallest unit in society consisting of husband and wife, or husband and wife and their children, or father and children, or mother and children, or blood relatives in direct lineage upward or downward up to the third degree.
8. Every person is an individual or corporation, whether a legal entity or not a legal entity.
9. Prevention is activities carried out to prevent the occurrence of acts of violence against women and children.
10. Protection is all efforts aimed at providing a sense of security to victims carried out by family, advocates, social institutions, police, prosecutors, courts or other parties either temporarily or based on court determination.
11. Women's Empowerment is a systematic and planned effort to achieve gender equality and justice in family and community life.
12. Gender responsive is a policy, program, activity and budgeting that takes into account differences in the needs, experiences and aspirations of men and women.
13. Violence is any act that results in or causes misery and suffering whether physical, sexual, psychological including threats of certain actions, coercion or arbitrary deprivation of freedom, whether occurring in public or in private life.
14. Victim is a woman and child who experiences misery and/or suffering either directly or indirectly as a result of violence.
15. Service is immediate activities and actions carried out by professional personnel in accordance with their respective professions in the form of counseling, therapy and advocacy for the strengthening and recovery of victims of violence.
16. Companion is a person or representative from an institution who has the expertise to provide assistance and has professional competence in their field.
17. Assistance is activities and actions carried out by companions during the service process.
18. Institution is an Office/Agency/Bureau within the scope of regional government and/or non-governmental organization (NGO) that provides assistance.
19. Integrated Service Center for Women's Empowerment and Children hereinafter referred to as PPTPPA, is an institution/functional work unit providing integrated services and assistance, counseling, referral and advocacy for women and children victims of violence.
20. Community is individuals, families, groups, social organizations and/or community organizations.

# BUPATI PASURUAN REGULATION
NUMBER 71 OF 2016

CONCERNING

AMENDMENT TO BUPATI PASURUAN REGULATION NUMBER 63 OF 2014 CONCERNING POSITION, ORGANIZATIONAL STRUCTURE, DUTIES AND FUNCTIONS AS WELL AS WORK PROCEDURES OF THE REGIONAL SECRETARIAT AND SECRETARIAT OF THE REGIONAL PEOPLE'S REPRESENTATIVE COUNCIL

WITH THE BLESSING OF GOD ALMIGHTY

BUPATI PASURUAN,

Considering : a. that in order to implement the provisions of Article 4 paragraph (2) of Government Regulation Number 18 of 2016 concerning Regional Apparatus, it is necessary to adjust the nomenclature of the Regional Secretariat organizational structure;

CHAPTER I
GENERAL PROVISIONS
Article 1
In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:
1. Region is Pasuruan Regency.
2. Regional Government is the Regional Government of Pasuruan Regency.
3. Regent is the Regent of Pasuruan.
4. Regional Apparatus Organization hereinafter abbreviated as OPD is the Regional Apparatus Organization within the Government of Pasuruan Regency.
5. Child is a person who has not reached the age of 18 (eighteen) years, including a child still in the womb.
6. Woman is a person (human being) who can menstruate, become pregnant, give birth to children and breastfeed.
7. Family is the smallest unit in society consisting of husband and wife, or husband and wife and their children, or father and children, or mother and children, or blood relatives in direct lineage upward or downward up to the third degree.
8. Every person is an individual or corporation, whether a legal entity or not a legal entity.
9. Prevention is activities carried out to prevent the occurrence of acts of violence against women and children.
10. Protection is all efforts aimed at providing a sense of security to victims carried out by family, advocates, social institutions, police, prosecutors, courts or other parties either temporarily or based on court determination.
11. Women's Empowerment is a systematic and planned effort to achieve gender equality and justice in family and community life.
12. Gender responsive is a policy, program, activity and budgeting that takes into account differences in the needs, experiences and aspirations of men and women.
13. Violence is any act that results in or causes misery and suffering whether physical, sexual, psychological including threats of certain actions, coercion or arbitrary deprivation of freedom, whether occurring in public or in private life.
14. Victim is a woman and child who experiences misery and/or suffering either directly or indirectly as a result of violence.
15. Service is immediate activities and actions carried out by professional personnel in accordance with their respective professions in the form of counseling, therapy and advocacy for the strengthening and recovery of victims of violence.
16. Companion is a person or representative from an institution who has the expertise to provide assistance and has professional competence in their field.
17. Assistance is activities and actions carried out by companions during the service process.
18. Institution is an Office/Agency/Bureau within the scope of regional government and/or non-governmental organization (NGO) that provides assistance.
19. Integrated Service Center for Women's Empowerment and Children hereinafter referred to as PPTPPA, is an institution/functional work unit providing integrated services and assistance, counseling, referral and advocacy for women and children victims of violence.
20. Community is individuals, families, groups, social organizations and/or community organizations.

CONCERNING
WOMEN'S EMPOWERMENT AND CHILD PROTECTION

I. GENERAL

The State as the mandate holder of people's sovereignty is responsible for implementing development to achieve community welfare. This is as mandated by the constitution which has become a national consensus for the Indonesian nation. The 1945 Constitution is the fundamental legal foundation (Fundamental Norm) in formulating the direction and basis for social, political, and state legal policy-making.

The State as an organization certainly always has objectives as stated in the fourth paragraph of the preamble of the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia which states: "Furthermore, to form a Government of the State of the Republic of Indonesia that protects the entire Indonesian nation and all Indonesian territory and to promote general welfare, educate the life of the nation, and participate in implementing world order based on freedom, eternal peace and social justice." Observing the fourth paragraph of the Preamble of the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia, it is clearly stated that this state was formed with the aim of protecting the entire nation and all Indonesian territory as well as improving the welfare of the people. This is also the objective of the formation of regional government which aims to accelerate the realization of community welfare through improvement, services, empowerment, and community participation, as well as increasing regional competitiveness by taking into account the principles of democracy, equity, justice, privileges and specificities of a region within the system of the Unitary State of the Republic of Indonesia.

Explicitly, the objectives of the Indonesian State reflect several national objectives of the Indonesian nation. The objectives contained in this fourth paragraph constitute the constitutional promise of the Indonesian state to all its people while simultaneously becoming the basic rights of the community. Therefore, the State is obligated to make various efforts in order to fulfill the constitutional rights of its citizens.

One of these four objectives is to protect the entire Indonesian nation and all Indonesian territory as well as promote general welfare. This means that the Indonesian nation must be free from all forms of actions that can harm its citizens, efforts to maintain this conduciveness are carried out in order to create a prosperous and beneficial social life without looking at certain groups and classes, because the meaning of the entire nation is a reflection for all Indonesian people without exception, whether men, women or children.

The protection that is the State's responsibility is not only for every person both in the individual and group sense along with the cultural identity attached to them, but this protection must also be interpreted as an endeavor to promote general welfare for the entire nation. Therefore, there need to be steps that must be taken by the State to achieve the above objectives by empowering its people, especially those who have been considered weak and marginalized. Based on these considerations, the Pasuruan Regency Government needs to establish a Regional Regulation on Women's Empowerment and Child Protection as a concrete step in order to protect the entire nation and promote general welfare.

From the above description, it is explicitly explained that based on article 18 of the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia, regional governments have the authority to make regulations related to regional needs in order to accommodate regional potential and local wisdom according to their respective localistic needs. Whereas for Pasuruan Regency, it has a distinctive character as a santri city that is strong with the values of its religious teachings. From the perspective of Islam, women's empowerment and child protection are highly upheld, even when Islam was first revealed to the Prophet Muhammad SAW. The condition of the Arab nation at that time greatly looked down upon the status of women. This can be proven by the existence of the custom of women as wives being able to be inherited to their children if their father died. Furthermore, for the fate of children at that time, it seemed that there was absolutely no protection of the rights given, children born with female gender would be killed by being buried alive because they were considered a disgrace to their parents. Departing from this condition, it is necessary to establish a regulation that reflects the values of women's empowerment and child protection.

Women's empowerment and child protection is a problem that needs to receive special attention from the Pasuruan Regency regional government to immediately create a juridical instrument to guard and ensure the guarantee of welfare and security for women and children.

Therefore, a legal umbrella in the form of a Regional Regulation is needed that is capable of accommodating all issues related to women's empowerment and child protection, capable of providing integrated services holistically and comprehensively, and explicitly giving mandates to institutions to coordinate policies and supervision, and mandates to institutions to provide services. In addition, the Regional Regulation can also open the involvement of non-governmental institutions and the community as well as the business world to play a broad role.

The implementation of women's empowerment and child protection in Pasuruan Regency does not yet have a strong legal basis in the form of regional regulations. Therefore, activities related to women's empowerment and child protection are carried out optimally in order to provide protection for women and children.

In relation to this, the Regional Regulation on women's empowerment and child protection is expected to anticipate and overcome all problems related to women's empowerment and child protection programs as well as become a juridical solution for regulations in Pasuruan Regency, so that it can provide protection and services to women and children in an integrated and comprehensive manner.

Observing the fourth paragraph of the Preamble of the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia, it is clearly stated that this state was formed with the aim of protecting the entire nation and all Indonesian territory as well as improving the welfare of the people. This is also the objective of the formation of regional government which aims to accelerate the realization of community welfare through improvement, services, empowerment, and community participation, as well as increasing regional competitiveness by taking into account the principles of democracy, equity, justice, privileges and specificities of a region within the system of the Unitary State of the Republic of Indonesia.

Departing from this condition, it is necessary to establish a regulation that reflects the values of women's empowerment and child protection.

Women's empowerment and child protection is a problem that needs to receive special attention from the Pasuruan Regency regional government to immediately create a juridical instrument to guard and ensure the guarantee of welfare and security for women and children.

The implementation of women's empowerment and child protection in Pasuruan Regency does not yet have a strong legal basis in the form of regional regulations. I. GENERAL

The State as the mandate holder of people's sovereignty is responsible for implementing development to achieve community welfare. This is as mandated by the constitution which has become a national consensus for the Indonesian nation. The 1945 Constitution is the fundamental legal foundation (Fundamental Norm) in formulating the direction and basis for social, political, and state legal policy-making.

The State as an organization certainly always has objectives as stated in the fourth paragraph of the preamble of the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia which states: "Furthermore, to form a Government of the State of the Republic of Indonesia that protects the entire Indonesian nation and all Indonesian territory and to promote general welfare, educate the life of the nation, and participate in implementing world order based on freedom, eternal peace and social justice." Observing the fourth paragraph of the Preamble of the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia, it is clearly stated that this state was formed with the aim of protecting the entire nation and all Indonesian territory as well as improving the welfare of the people. This is also the objective of the formation of regional government which aims to accelerate the realization of community welfare through improvement, services, empowerment, and community participation, as well as increasing regional competitiveness by taking into account the principles of democracy, equity, justice, privileges and specificities of a region within the system of the Unitary State of the Republic of Indonesia.

Explicitly, the objectives of the Indonesian State reflect several national objectives of the Indonesian nation. The objectives contained in this fourth paragraph constitute the constitutional promise of the Indonesian state to all its people while simultaneously becoming the basic rights of the community. Therefore, the State is obligated to make various efforts in order to fulfill the constitutional rights of its citizens.

One of these four objectives is to protect the entire Indonesian nation and all Indonesian territory as well as promote general welfare. This means that the Indonesian nation must be free from all forms of actions that can harm its citizens, efforts to maintain this conduciveness are carried out in order to create a prosperous and beneficial social life without looking at certain groups and classes, because the meaning of the entire nation is a reflection for all Indonesian people without exception, whether men, women or children.

The protection that is the State's responsibility is not only for every person both in the individual and group sense along with the cultural identity attached to them, but this protection must also be interpreted as an endeavor to promote general welfare for the entire nation. Therefore, there need to be steps that must be taken by the State to achieve the above objectives by empowering its people, especially those who have been considered weak and marginalized. From the above description, it is explicitly explained that based on article 18 of the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia, regional governments have the authority to make regulations related to regional needs in order to accommodate regional potential and local wisdom according to their respective localistic needs. Whereas for Pasuruan Regency, it has a distinctive character as a santri city that is strong with the values of its religious teachings. From the perspective of Islam, women's empowerment and child protection are highly upheld, even when Islam was first revealed to the Prophet Muhammad SAW. The condition of the Arab nation at that time greatly looked down upon the status of women. This can be proven by the existence of the custom of women as wives being able to be inherited to their children if their father died. Furthermore, for the fate of children at that time, it seemed that there was absolutely no protection of the rights given, children born with female gender would be killed by being buried alive because they were considered a disgrace to their parents. Departing from this condition, it is necessary to establish a regulation that reflects the values of women's empowerment and child protection.

Women's empowerment and child protection is a problem that needs to receive special attention from the Pasuruan Regency regional government to immediately create a juridical instrument to guard and ensure the guarantee of welfare and security for women and children.

Therefore, a legal umbrella in the form of a Regional Regulation is needed that is capable of accommodating all issues related to women's empowerment and child protection, capable of providing integrated services holistically and comprehensively, and explicitly giving mandates to institutions to coordinate policies and supervision, and mandates to institutions to provide services. In addition, the Regional Regulation can also open the involvement of non-governmental institutions and the community as well as the business world to play a broad role.

The implementation of women's empowerment and child protection in Pasuruan Regency does not yet have a strong legal basis in the form of regional regulations. Therefore, activities related to women's empowerment and child protection are carried out optimally in order to provide protection for women and children.

In relation to this, the Regional Regulation on women's empowerment and child protection is expected to anticipate and overcome all problems related to women's empowerment and child protection programs as well as become a juridical solution for regulations in Pasuruan Regency, so that it can provide protection and services to women and children in an integrated and comprehensive manner.

EXPLANATION
O F
REGIONAL REGULATION OF PASURUAN REGENCY
NUMBER 4 YEAR 2018
CONCERNING
WOMEN'S EMPOWERMENT AND CHILD PROTECTION

I. GENERAL

The State as the mandate holder of people's sovereignty is responsible for implementing development to achieve community welfare. This is as mandated by the constitution which has become a national consensus for the Indonesian nation. The 1945 Constitution is the fundamental legal foundation (Fundamental Norm) in formulating the direction and basis for social, political, and state legal policy-making.

The State as an organization certainly always has objectives as stated in the fourth paragraph of the preamble of the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia which states: "Furthermore, to form a Government of the State of the Republic of Indonesia that protects the entire Indonesian nation and all Indonesian territory and to promote general welfare, educate the life of the nation, and participate in implementing world order based on freedom, eternal peace and social justice." Observing the fourth paragraph of the Preamble of the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia, it is clearly stated that this state was formed with the aim of protecting the entire nation and all Indonesian territory as well as improving the welfare of the people. This is also the objective of the formation of regional government which aims to accelerate the realization of community welfare through improvement, services, empowerment, and community participation, as well as increasing regional competitiveness by taking into account the principles of democracy, equity, justice, privileges and specificities of a region within the system of the Unitary State of the Republic of Indonesia.

Explicitly, the objectives of the Indonesian State reflect several national objectives of the Indonesian nation. The objectives contained in this fourth paragraph constitute the constitutional promise of the Indonesian state to all its people while simultaneously becoming the basic rights of the community. Therefore, the State is obligated to make various efforts in order to fulfill the constitutional rights of its citizens.

One of these four objectives is to protect the entire Indonesian nation and all Indonesian territory as well as promote general welfare. This means that the Indonesian nation must be free from all forms of actions that can harm its citizens, efforts to maintain this conduciveness are carried out in order to create a prosperous and beneficial social life without looking at certain groups and classes, because the meaning of the entire nation is a reflection for all Indonesian people without exception, whether men, women or children.

The protection that is the State's responsibility is not only for every person both in the individual and group sense along with the cultural identity attached to them, but this protection must also be interpreted as an endeavor to promote general welfare for the entire nation. Therefore, there need to be steps that must be taken by the State to achieve the above objectives by empowering its people, especially those who have been considered weak and marginalized. Based on these considerations, the Pasuruan Regency Government needs to establish a Regional Regulation on Women's Empowerment and Child Protection as a concrete step in order to protect the entire nation and promote general welfare.

From the above description, it is explicitly explained that based on article 18 of the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia, regional governments have the authority to make regulations related to regional needs in order to accommodate regional potential and local wisdom according to their respective localistic needs. Whereas for Pasuruan Regency, it has a distinctive character as a santri city that is strong with the values of its religious teachings. From the perspective of Islam, women's empowerment and child protection are highly upheld, even when Islam was first revealed to the Prophet Muhammad SAW. The condition of the Arab nation at that time greatly looked down upon the status of women. This can be proven by the existence of the custom of women as wives being able to be inherited to their children if their father died. Furthermore, for the fate of children at that time, it seemed that there was absolutely no protection of the rights given, children born with female gender would be killed by being buried alive because they were considered a disgrace to their parents. Departing from this condition, it is necessary to establish a regulation that reflects the values of women's empowerment and child protection.

Women's empowerment and child protection is a problem that needs to receive special attention from the Pasuruan Regency regional government to immediately create a juridical instrument to guard and ensure the guarantee of welfare and security for women and children.

Therefore, a legal umbrella in the form of a Regional Regulation is needed that is capable of accommodating all issues related to women's empowerment and child protection, capable of providing integrated services holistically and comprehensively, and explicitly giving mandates to institutions to coordinate policies and supervision, and mandates to institutions to provide services. In addition, the Regional Regulation can also open the involvement of non-governmental institutions and the community as well as the business world to play a broad role.

The implementation of women's empowerment and child protection in Pasuruan Regency does not yet have a strong legal basis in the form of regional regulations. Therefore, activities related to women's empowerment and child protection are carried out optimally in order to provide protection for women and children.

In relation to this, the Regional Regulation on women's empowerment and child protection is expected to anticipate and overcome all problems related to women's empowerment and child protection programs as well as become a juridical solution for regulations in Pasuruan Regency, so that it can provide protection and services to women and children in an integrated and comprehensive manner.
